name: Open-NCR refusal of submission for completion approval
description: One refusal shape returned by every code path that can put a traveler forward for completion approval — status 'submitted for completion' (1.5), or status 'completed' (2) reached directly from 'active' (1) — while any linked NCR is not Closed (spec FR-013 to FR-016). Produced by lib/traveler-ncr.js assertNoOpenNcrs(); the three call sites below all return it unchanged. No role, including administrators and managers, bypasses it (FR-015). The rule is enforced at submission only: reviewer approval and 1.5 -> 2 are deliberately NOT gated, because NCR initiation requires an active traveler (FR-009) so none can be opened after submission (spec Assumptions).

applies_to.when: req.body.status is 1.5 (after the existing transition and authorization checks, before the save). This route's shared stateTransition table does not allow 1 -> 2.
req.body.status is 1.5 (same stateTransition table, so 1 -> 2 is not reachable here)

body.status parses to 1.5, OR to 2 while the traveler's current status is 1 (the helper's case 2 accepts 1 -> 2 directly, which would otherwise skip submission). Checked before updateTravelerStatus runs.

body.message: This traveler cannot be submitted for completion approval while 2 linked NCRs are not Closed.

open_ncrs.status: string — one of Submitted | Dispositioned | Approval Requested | Returned for Comment | Final Approval
open_ncrs.input_name: string | null — null for a legacy link with no input

client_behaviour.public/javascripts/traveler.js setStatus: On 409 with code OPEN_NCRS render an alert listing each NCR as a link (prefix + '/ncrs/' + ncr_id) with its status and input label. Build with DOM/.text(); never concatenate response text into HTML. Other failures keep the existing 'Cannot change the status: ...' text.
client_behaviour.public/javascripts/traveler.js complete: Called by the 'Submit for completion' button (#complete2). It disables the form inputs before calling setStatus(1.5); re-enable them when the request fails.

not_refused: 1.5 -> 2 (approval, including reviewer approval via lib/review.js) — not gated (spec Assumptions)
1.5 -> 1 (rejection back to active); the traveler is checked again on its next submission (spec US3 scenario 5)
1 -> 1.5 when every linked NCR is Closed, or the traveler has none (spec FR-016; the traveler's other submission and approval rules are unchanged)
